title: How to use the parental controls on iOS 27
description: Following the release of its September operating system updates, Apple has overhauled its Screen Time parental controls across its ecosystem. Developed alongside the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), the refreshed features aim…
fullText:
Following the release of its September operating system updates, Apple has overhauled its Screen Time parental controls across its ecosystem. Developed alongside the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), the refreshed features aim to help guardians balance their children’s digital engagement with schoolwork, physical activity, sleep, and family commitments. The initiative also includes an official companion guide titled Building Healthy Digital Habits to support families with ongoing guidance.

The updated system replaces traditional App Limits with more flexible Time Allowances. Rather than setting individual timers on dozens of specific applications, guardians can establish broader daily limits and distribute hours across specific groupings such as social media, gaming, or entertainment, as well as bespoke custom categories. Setting up a child’s profile has also been streamlined, serving age-tailored app suggestions instead of installing every default programme across the home screen.

Safety protections across Apple’s communication and browsing tools have seen substantial upgrades. A new Ask to Browse setting requires young users to seek approval via Messages before visiting unapproved websites on Safari, whilst Ask to Add Contacts mandates parental sign-off before a child can call or message unfamiliar phone numbers. Furthermore, Communication Safety has been expanded beyond nudity detection to identify and blur scenes of graphic violence and gore across FaceTime, AirDrop, and Messages. Parents can also temporarily lock a child's screen instantly using a new Pause Device function.

To access the refreshed Screen Time tools, households must ensure every iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple TV in their Family Sharing group runs its respective version 27 operating system. Devices unable to upgrade will remain on legacy software, which creates an operational gap across older hardware. Initial setups apply stricter defaults, including automatic web and contact approvals for users under 13, alongside universal content blurring for all minors under 18.

title: Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial
description: United States President Donald Trump has launched a concerted effort to rebrand artificial intelligence across the federal government, insisting that the sector instead be known as "super intelligence". Following an address at…
fullText:
United States President Donald Trump has launched a concerted effort to rebrand artificial intelligence across the federal government, insisting that the sector instead be known as "super intelligence". Following an address at the United Nations last month where he claimed the word "artificial" makes the technology sound fake, Trump signed an executive order barring the use of "AI" wherever possible. He subsequently escalated the rhetoric, warning that the White House regards anyone still using the term artificial intelligence as "THE ENEMY".

The administration's linguistic mandate has triggered rapid revisions across government bodies. The US Center for AI Standards and Innovation has been retitled the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence. Additionally, the Department of Justice has altered its communication materials, recently retroactively classifying a long-running streaming fraud scheme as "Super Intelligence-Assisted Music Streaming Fraud".

Prominent leaders across the technology sector have largely fallen in line with the decree. Elon Musk committed to changing the name of SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, whilst Jeff Bezos voiced support, noting that the word artificial is unflattering. Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and OpenAI leader Sam Altman have similarly endorsed the shift, although Altman confirmed that OpenAI would not alter its corporate moniker. Concurrently, Trump has begun utilising "artificial" as a broader slur, retiring the phrase "fake news media" to brand the press "artificial media".

This state-mandated shift matters because it artificially blurs critical technical distinctions within computer science. Historically, the single word "superintelligence" specifically described hypothetical, highly advanced systems capable of exceeding human cognitive capabilities, rather than commonplace automation or music-generation tools. Applying the term universally dilutes the marketing power of future breakthroughs. Furthermore, Trump faces hurdles across other government branches, as he cannot stop Congress from using the original phrase, which remains codified in existing federal statutes that government agencies must uphold in court.

title: Five people shot and killed in apparent murder-suicide, Georgia police say
description: Five members of the same family have died following a suspected murder-suicide at a residence in Douglas, south Georgia. Emergency services attended the property on Friday after receiving an active shooter alert,…
fullText:
Five members of the same family have died following a suspected murder-suicide at a residence in Douglas, south Georgia. Emergency services attended the property on Friday after receiving an active shooter alert, which had been placed by one of the victims.

Upon entering the house, police discovered the bodies of four adults who had sustained fatal gunshot wounds. A fifth person was taken to a local hospital for emergency treatment, but was subsequently pronounced dead. Authorities have not yet disclosed the precise sequence of events or identified who among the household fired the shots, noting that the broader circumstances remain under formal investigation.

Law enforcement revealed that an earlier emergency call had been logged from the residence hours before the fatal gunfire took place. During that prior contact, a woman residing at the address reported to police that her husband’s smoking was killing her. Following that initial complaint, emergency medical staff conveyed the woman to a nearby medical centre.

Speaking at a media conference on Saturday, Douglas Police Chief Brannen Pruette acknowledged the deep distress the deaths have caused within the local community, appealing to the public to afford the surviving relatives privacy whilst they mourn. Police have kept further operational findings confidential as inquiries into the case proceed.

The event marks the second apparent murder-suicide in the area within a span of three months, according to Douglas City Manager Charlie Davis. Addressing the broader context of the incident, Davis highlighted the pervasive nature of domestic violence, remarking that it transcends race, religion, and geographic location. He urged residents to avoid unverified speculation surrounding the tragedy, which coincided with another lethal family shooting and suicide reported in Pennsylvania on the same day.
